title: UP BOARD CLASS 9 — Social Science | Drainage Rivers India
description: Subject-wise test on Drainage Rivers India (Social Science) for UP BOARD CLASS 9. 40Q.
subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest peninsular river in India, both in terms of its length and the area of its drainage basin?

options.explanation: Krishna is a major peninsular river but not the largest.
Godavari is the largest peninsular river in terms of length and drainage area.
Mahanadi is a significant river but smaller in length and drainage area compared to Godavari.
Narmada is a west-flowing river but not the largest peninsular river.

questions.explanation: The Godavari River is often referred to as the 'Dakshin Ganga' due to its length and large drainage basin, making it the largest among the peninsular rivers.
questions.hint: This river is also known as the 'Dakshin Ganga'.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Which two major rivers flow westwards and form estuaries instead of deltas?

options.explanation: Godavari and Krishna flow eastwards and form deltas.
Narmada and Tapi flow westwards and form estuaries.
Mahanadi and Kaveri flow eastwards and form deltas.
Ganga and Yamuna are Himalayan rivers flowing eastwards.

questions.explanation: The Narmada and Tapi (or Tapti) rivers are the only major peninsular rivers that flow westwards into the Arabian Sea and form estuaries because they flow through rift valleys.
questions.hint: These rivers flow through rift valleys and empty into the Arabian Sea.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: The River Ganga originates from which glacier?

options.explanation: Siachen Glacier is located in the Karakoram range and is not the origin of the Ganga.
Gangotri Glacier is the source of the Bhagirathi, which forms the Ganga.
Yamunotri Glacier is the source of the Yamuna river.
Pindari Glacier is the source of the Pindar river, a tributary of the Alaknanda.

questions.explanation: The Ganga river originates as the Bhagirathi from the Gangotri Glacier in the Himalayas.
questions.hint: This glacier is located in the Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Wular Lake in Jammu and Kashmir is an example of which type of lake?

options.explanation: Saline lakes have high salt content, unlike Wular Lake.
Ox-bow lakes are formed by meandering rivers cutting off loops.
Wular Lake is formed due to tectonic movements in the Earth's crust.
Lagoons are formed by the action of waves and currents along coasts.

questions.explanation: Wular Lake is the largest freshwater lake in India and is a result of tectonic activity.
questions.hint: This type of lake is formed due to movements in the Earth's crust.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a tributary of the River Ganga?

options.explanation: Yamuna is a major tributary of the Ganga.
Kosi is a major tributary of the Ganga.
Son is a major tributary of the Ganga.
Tapi is a west-flowing river and not a tributary of the Ganga.

questions.explanation: Yamuna, Kosi, and Son are all major tributaries of the River Ganga. Tapi (or Tapti) is a west-flowing peninsular river that drains into the Arabian Sea.
questions.hint: This river flows westwards and is not part of the Ganga basin.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: A drainage pattern where the river channel follows the slope of the terrain, and the tributaries join the main river at acute angles, resembling the branches of a tree, is known as:

options.explanation: Trellis drainage pattern occurs where rivers flow parallel to each other and join at right angles.
Rectangular drainage pattern occurs where rivers flow along fractures or joints in the rock.
Dendritic drainage pattern resembles the branches of a tree.
Radial drainage pattern occurs when rivers flow outward from a central high point.

questions.explanation: The dendritic drainage pattern develops where the river channel follows the slope of the terrain, and the tributaries join the main river at acute angles, creating a tree-like appearance.
questions.hint: This pattern resembles the branching of a tree.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE about Himalayan rivers compared to Peninsular rivers?

options.text: Himalayan rivers are seasonal, while Peninsular rivers are perennial.
options.explanation: Himalayan rivers are perennial, while Peninsular rivers are largely seasonal.

options.text: Himalayan rivers flow through shallow valleys, while Peninsular rivers flow through deep gorges.
options.explanation: Himalayan rivers flow through deep gorges, while Peninsular rivers flow through shallow valleys.

options.text: Himalayan rivers are mostly perennial, receiving water from snowmelt and rainfall.
options.explanation: Himalayan rivers are perennial due to snowmelt and rainfall.

options.text: Peninsular rivers are typically longer and have larger catchments than Himalayan rivers.
options.explanation: Peninsular rivers are generally shorter and have smaller catchments compared to Himalayan rivers.

questions.explanation: Himalayan rivers are perennial because they are fed by both snowmelt from glaciers and rainfall. Peninsular rivers are largely seasonal and rain-fed, flow through comparatively shallower valleys, and are generally shorter.
questions.hint: Himalayan rivers are fed by both snowmelt and rainfall, making them perennial.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: The 'Sunderban Delta', the world's largest and fastest-growing delta, is formed by which two major rivers?

options.explanation: Narmada and Tapi flow westwards and do not form the Sunderban Delta.
Godavari and Krishna flow eastwards and form their own deltas.
Ganga and Brahmaputra form the Sunderban Delta.
Mahanadi and Godavari form separate deltas.

questions.explanation: The Sunderban Delta is formed by the confluence of the Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers before they empty into the Bay of Bengal.
questions.hint: This delta is located in West Bengal and Bangladesh.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Assertion (A): The Peninsular rivers have shorter and shallower courses as compared to Himalayan rivers. Reason (R): Peninsular rivers originate from the Peninsular plateau and are largely dependent on rainfall, leading to fluctuating water levels.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true. The fact that Peninsular rivers originate from the plateau and are rain-fed directly explains why their courses are shorter, shallower, and have fluctuating water levels compared to the perennial, snow-fed Himalayan rivers.
questions.hint: Both the assertion and reason are correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.question: A river originates from a glacier in the Himalayas, flows westwards through a magnificent gorge, enters Pakistan near Chilas, and eventually empties into the Arabian Sea. Which of the following rivers is being described?

options.explanation: Ganga flows eastwards and empties into the Bay of Bengal.
Brahmaputra flows eastwards and then southwards into the Bay of Bengal.
Indus matches the description provided.
Yamuna is a tributary of the Ganga and flows eastwards.

questions.explanation: The description perfectly matches the Indus River. It originates in the Tibetan Himalayas (near Mansarovar Lake), flows westwards through a gorge, enters Pakistan, and drains into the Arabian Sea.
questions.hint: This river is one of the longest rivers in Asia and flows through India and Pakistan.

questions.question: Which of the following is the longest river in India, flowing entirely within the country?

options.explanation: Brahmaputra flows through India and Bangladesh, not entirely within India.
Ganga is a major river but not the longest entirely within India.
Godavari is the longest river flowing entirely within India.
Indus flows through India and Pakistan, not entirely within India.

questions.explanation: While Ganga is a major river, and Brahmaputra and Indus are longer overall, the Godavari is the longest river that flows entirely within India. It is often referred to as the 'Dakshin Ganga'.
questions.hint: Consider rivers that do not flow outside India's borders.

questions.question: The Ganga river originates from which glacier?

options.explanation: Siachen Glacier is located in the Karakoram range and is not associated with the Ganga.
Pindari Glacier is a smaller glacier in Uttarakhand but not the source of the Ganga.
Gangotri Glacier is the source of the Bhagirathi, a headstream of the Ganga.
Yamunotri Glacier is the source of the Yamuna river, not the Ganga.

questions.explanation: The main headstream of the Ganga, known as Bhagirathi, originates from the Gangotri Glacier at Gaumukh in Uttarakhand.
questions.hint: Look for the glacier located in Uttarakhand associated with the Ganga.

questions.question: Which of the following Peninsular rivers flows westward into the Arabian Sea?

options.explanation: Mahanadi flows eastward into the Bay of Bengal.
Godavari flows eastward into the Bay of Bengal.
Krishna flows eastward into the Bay of Bengal.
Narmada is a major Peninsular river flowing westward into the Arabian Sea.

questions.explanation: The Narmada and Tapi are the two major Peninsular rivers that flow westward and drain into the Arabian Sea, forming estuaries. The others flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal.
questions.hint: Identify rivers that flow towards the west coast of India.

questions.question: The Sunderban Delta, the world's largest delta, is formed by the confluence of which two major river systems?

options.explanation: Godavari and Krishna flow into the Bay of Bengal but do not form the Sunderban Delta.
Narmada and Tapi flow westward into the Arabian Sea.
Ganga and Brahmaputra merge to form the Sunderban Delta.
Indus and Jhelum flow through Pakistan and do not form the Sunderban Delta.

questions.explanation: The Sunderban Delta is formed by the mighty Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers (known as Padma and Jamuna respectively in Bangladesh) as they merge before draining into the Bay of Bengal.
questions.hint: Consider the two major rivers that merge in the Bengal region to form the delta.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest freshwater lake in India, located in Jammu and Kashmir?

options.explanation: Sambhar Lake is a saltwater lake in Rajasthan.
Wular Lake is the largest freshwater lake in India, located in Jammu and Kashmir.
Chilika Lake is a brackish water lagoon in Odisha.
Pulicat Lake is a brackish water lagoon in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

questions.explanation: Wular Lake is the largest freshwater lake in India. Sambhar is a saltwater lake, and Chilika and Pulicat are brackish water lagoons.
questions.hint: Look for the largest freshwater lake in Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.question: A river basin in India is known for its extensive network of tributaries, including the Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej. This river system is primarily located in the northern and northwestern parts of India. Identify the main river of this system.

options.explanation: Ganga's major tributaries include Yamuna, Ghaghara, and Gandak, not Chenab, Ravi, Beas, or Sutlej.
Brahmaputra's tributaries include Subansiri, Manas, and Teesta, not the ones mentioned.
Indus has five major tributaries: Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej, and Jhelum.
Yamuna is a tributary of the Ganga, not the main river of this system.

questions.explanation: The description clearly points to the Indus River System, which has these five major tributaries (the 'Panchnad') flowing through Punjab and draining into the Indus.
questions.hint: Consider the major river system in northern and northwestern India with these tributaries.

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics is *not* typical of Peninsular rivers?

options.text: They are mostly seasonal or non-perennial.
options.explanation: This is a typical characteristic of Peninsular rivers.

options.text: They have shorter and shallower courses.
options.explanation: This is a typical characteristic of Peninsular rivers.

options.text: They form large deltas at their mouths on the Arabian Sea coast.
options.explanation: Peninsular rivers flowing into the Arabian Sea form estuaries, not large deltas.

options.text: Their valleys are generally well-adjusted and graded.
options.explanation: This is a typical characteristic of Peninsular rivers.

questions.explanation: Peninsular rivers that flow into the Arabian Sea (like Narmada and Tapi) do *not* form large deltas; instead, they form estuaries due to the hard rock terrain and the relatively steep gradient near their mouths. Rivers flowing into the Bay of Bengal (e.g., Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri) do form deltas.
questions.hint: Identify the incorrect characteristic of Peninsular rivers.

questions.question: Consider a river that originates in the Tibetan Plateau, flows eastward parallel to the Himalayas, enters India in Arunachal Pradesh, and is known for its high volume of water and frequent floods in Assam. Which river is being described?

options.explanation: Indus flows westward and does not enter India in Arunachal Pradesh.
Ganga originates in the Himalayas and flows southward, not eastward parallel to the Himalayas.
Brahmaputra fits the description perfectly.
Mahanadi flows eastward but originates in the Eastern Ghats, not the Tibetan Plateau.

questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra river originates in Tibet (where it is known as Tsangpo), flows eastward, takes a U-turn to enter India through Arunachal Pradesh (where it is called Dihang), and then flows through Assam, where it is known for its large volume of water and devastating floods.
questions.hint: Look for a river that flows through Arunachal Pradesh and Assam with a high volume of water.
